page.metaTitle: Website Monitoring for E-commerce Brands | WebMonitor.fyi
page.metaDescription: Website monitoring for e-commerce: track competitor pricing, watch for MAP violations, monitor reviews, and catch site downtime. One platform, every signal.
page.subtitle: Catch competitor pricing changes, MAP violations, review activity, and site outages from one dashboard built for retail and DTC teams.
page.intro: E-commerce teams juggle a lot of signals at once: competitor pricing, third-party seller activity, customer reviews, supply availability, paid-ad landing-page uptime. Most teams end up spread across five or six tools to cover it. WebMonitor.fyi runs the monitoring layer in one place. Used by Shopify brands, Amazon sellers, DTC startups, and multi-channel retailers from solo founders to teams of 50+.

challenges.title: Competitor price tracking at scale
challenges.body: When you have 200 SKUs and three competitors, manual price checks are impossible. Automated monitoring with plain-English criteria handles the scale without a data team.

challenges.title: MAP (minimum advertised price) enforcement
challenges.body: For brands selling through third-party resellers, MAP violations show up daily on Amazon and Walmart marketplaces. Daily monitoring catches violations fast enough to enforce.

challenges.title: Inventory and restock visibility
challenges.body: Out-of-stock products on your top retailers cost real revenue. Restock alerts on key SKUs catch lapses before they spread.

challenges.title: Review monitoring across platforms
challenges.body: Amazon reviews, Trustpilot, Google Business — each platform has its own response window. Real-time alerts mean responses happen within the window, not days later.

challenges.title: Launch-day uptime
challenges.body: A product launch with a Klaviyo email blast at 9am can pull traffic that exposes any weak point in the checkout funnel. One-minute uptime checks during launch windows catch issues fast.

page.limits: WebMonitor watches the public surface — product pages, pricing pages, public review pages, marketplace listings. Anything behind a seller-only login (Amazon Brand Registry analytics, Shopify admin data, wholesale-portal pricing) needs a dedicated integration. Personalized pricing that varies per logged-in shopper is also outside what a public-page check can see.

faq.q: Can I track my own product across multiple marketplaces?
faq.a: Yes — one monitor per listing per marketplace. The dashboard groups them by SKU so you see Amazon, Walmart, Target, and your own Shopify store side by side.

faq.q: Does this work with private-label or Amazon-exclusive brands?
faq.a: Yes. Public Amazon listings work whether the brand is private-label, branded, or unbranded. For Amazon Brand Registry-specific tooling (which uses an authenticated API), WebMonitor complements rather than replaces it — most brands run both.

faq.q: How do I monitor a product that's currently out of stock?
faq.a: The monitor still polls the page. Set the criterion to "alert me when this product is back in stock" — the alert fires the moment the page state flips from unavailable to available.

faq.q: Can the customer-success team get a Slack alert on every new negative review?
faq.a: Yes. Set the criterion to "alert me on any review under 4 stars" and route the webhook into a #reviews channel. The team typically responds within hours of the alert.
